title: policy-driven structural regression detector for config rollouts
creator: Jordan Reyes
description: Build a policy-driven regression detector that flags degradations in structured JSON outputs caused by model or config rollouts. This ticket covers design + prototype for a detector that combines multi-anchor behavioral diffs, per-field tolerance bands, and config-aware weighting to surface actionable regressions during canary and gradual rollouts. The goal is to reduce false positives from innocuous shape/ordering differences while catching regressions that affect downstream consumers (parsers, embeddings, DB writes).
acceptance_criteria: A detector prototype that runs on rollout traffic (canary + 10% shard) and produces a ranked list of regression signals within 30 minutes of rollout start
Per-field metrics computed: presence rate delta, type-coercion rate, enum drift, value-distribution shift (KS/p-value), and sample-wise structural diffs
Config-aware scoring: detector weights signal contributions by config changes (temperature, max_tokens, model_id, quantization) and surfaces the most likely root cause
False positive rate below 5% on historical rollouts (measured against labeled post-rollout investigations)
An initial runbook and dashboard prototype (console) that lets PMs/SEs inspect examples, aggregated stats, and suggested rollback confidence
metrics: precision@k for top-5 signals vs. engineer triage
implementation_notes: Ingest canary and baseline traffic into evaluation job: store tokenized outputs + schema-parsed AST for efficient diffs
Compute field-level stats with configurable tolerance bands; use both absolute and relative thresholds
Implement multi-anchor baseline: recent stable prod, last-known-good rollout, and synthetic golden set
Weight signals by config delta — changes to model_id and temperature get higher prior weight than prompt-affecting flags
Use reservoir sampling for example storage to keep bounded memory while preserving rare edge cases
Expose a small REST endpoint to accept 'explain' requests that return top contributing tokens/fields for a signal
Integration plan: pilot on 2 product routes (chat-completion, structured-ordering) then expand to embeddings pipelines
comments: 2025-02-18 - Jordan Reyes: Kickoff doc attached. Primary concern is balancing sensitivity vs. noise for benign formatting changes. Initial approach: per-field KS tests and a presence-rate delta heuristic.

2025-02-22 - Mei Chen: Implemented baseline ingestion job for canary traffic. Observed heavy variance on 'notes' free-text field; plan to treat long free-text as out-of-scope for structural detector and rely on semantic evals instead.

2025-02-26 - Priya Natarajan (PM): Suggest adding config-priority table mapping (e.g., model_id, quantization, max_seq) so the detector can downweight low-impact flags. Also requested example UI wireframe for triage flow.

2025-03-01 - Mei Chen: Prototype produces per-field deltas and ranks signals. Found spike in enum drift when switching to model variant rwd-2b-quant; dumping top 10 failing samples to Google Drive for triage.

2025-03-03 - Eng review: Agreed to add synthetic perturbation tests (mutations of golden examples) to estimate expected false positive band. Decided to keep initial run window to 30 minutes and iterate on thresholds after pilot. Action: create dashboard ticket and storage pruning job.
